newsitem.title: UK: UK buy-outs a record 7.5 billion stg in 1996 - study.
newsitem.headline: UK buy-outs a record 7.5 billion stg in 1996 - study.

text.p: Britain's buy-out market reached a record 7.5 billion stg in 1996, up 39 percent from last year, according to a study released on Monday.
The Centre for Management Buy-Out Research said the total value of buy-outs and buy-ins in 1996 was 51 million stg greater than in 1989, the previous record year.
The study also predicted that uncertainty surrounding Britain's next general election, due by May, could lead to high levels of activity before then.

"Demand for buy-outs and buy-ins from both managers and investors, coupled with market liquidity, should ensure a steady and continuing flow of transactions at the level of the last six months," the study said.
The number of transactions rose by seven percent in 1996 compared with 1995 to 619.
That total beat 1990's record by 19 deals, the study said.
This year, only 53 transactions worth over 25 million stg took place, representing just 8.5 percent of the total.
"The vast majority of buy-outs and buy-ins are therefore below 25 million stg, a segment of the market that offers good opportunities for management teams," the centre's study said.
The centre was founded by Deloitte & Touche and BZW at the University of Nottingham.
Earlier on Monday, accountants KPMG put the total for buy-outs and buy-ins in 1996 at 6.77 billion stg. KPMG agreed that 1996 was a record year.
